CHIEF COMPLAINT
Evaluation of kidneys given Smith-Magenis Syndrome diagnosis.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Katherine is a 22-month-old female with Smith-Magenis Syndrome, diagnosed by her neurologist. She is a twin; her twin sister is unaffected and developing normally. Katherine was born at 34 weeks and 3 days gestation with a birth weight of 4 pounds 8 ounces; her twin sister weighed 3 pounds 13 ounces. As a newborn, Katherine had feeding difficulties with associated apnea during eating and difficulty regulating temperature. She has severe reflux and sees a GI doctor. She was taken off cow's milk by a dietician and now drinks ripple pea protein milk and water. She has been evaluated by multiple specialists including an allergist, neurologist, orthopedic surgeon, ophthalmologist, and audiologist. Developmentally, she was not sitting independently by one year of age and does not walk independently, but is now crawling and attempting to take steps. She is enrolled in feeding therapy, occupational therapy, and physical therapy, with speech therapy beginning within the next couple of weeks. She has 8 to 10 wet diapers in a 24-hour period and drinks frequently. The family was referred to nephrology as Smith-Magenis Syndrome can be associated with congenital anomalies of the kidney and urinary tract. The family lives in Dallas, Georgia.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Patient has history of feeding difficulties with apnea while eating and severe reflux. Developmental delay in motor milestones noted. No acute symptoms reported at this visit.

FAMILY HISTORY
Older sibling, a 9-year-old son, with autism. Twin sister is unaffected. No family history of kidney failure, dialysis, or transplantation.

SOCIAL HISTORY
Family resides in Dallas, Georgia.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Well-nourished female, slightly fussy when examined. Eyes small appearing. Mild hypotonia of lower extremities and arms. Normal external female genitalia.

RESULTS
Not discussed.

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
Katherine is a 22-month-old female, born at 34 weeks 3 days gestation, with Smith-Magenis Syndrome. Smith-Magenis Syndrome is a chromosomal deletion syndrome that can affect multiple organ systems. Congenital anomalies of the kidney and urinary tract have been reported in association with this syndrome. Plan: Kidney ultrasound to be obtained today. Doctor will call patient with results. If ultrasound is normal, patient will not require further nephrology follow-up. If ultrasound is abnormal, patient can follow up in Kennesaw and next steps will be determined. Since family resides in Dallas, Georgia, follow-up should be coordinated at town center location.
